Tidy vector geometry verbs

geo-vector.Rd

Native tidyverse-style wrappers around common sf operations. Inputs accept sf tables or data frames with lon/lat (converted with geo_as_sf()); outputs are sf tibbles. sf reads and writes through GDAL/OGR, so GeoPackage, shapefile, GeoJSON and similar formats work via geo_vector_read() / geo_vector_write() without calling GDAL utilities or the retired rgdal package. Prefer GeoPackage over shapefile for new work.

Usage

geo_buffer(data, dist, lon = lon, lat = lat, ...)

geo_intersection(data, y, lon = lon, lat = lat, ...)

geo_difference(data, y, lon = lon, lat = lat, ...)

geo_union(data, y = NULL, lon = lon, lat = lat, ...)

geo_crop(data, y, lon = lon, lat = lat, ...)

geo_area(data, lon = lon, lat = lat)

geo_centroid(data, lon = lon, lat = lat)

geo_bbox(data, lon = lon, lat = lat)

geo_join(
  data,
  y,
  join = c("intersects", "within", "contains", "nearest"),
  lon = lon,
  lat = lat,
  ...
)

geo_distance_to(data, to, lon = lon, lat = lat, ...)

Arguments

data

An sf object or a data frame with coordinates.

dist

Buffer distance. For geographic CRS, metres (passed through sf::st_buffer with sf::st_transform to an equidistant projection when needed).

lon, lat

Coordinate columns when data is not sf.

...

Passed to the underlying sf helper.

y

Second geometry table for binary operations and joins.

join

Spatial predicate for geo_join(): "intersects", "within", "contains", or "nearest".

to

Geometry or coordinates to measure distance to.

Examples

sites <- geo_as_sf(geo_example_sites("wilhelm"), lon, lat)
buf <- geo_buffer(sites, dist = 5000)
geo_area(buf)
